name: Client-side image compressor
description: Image compression is one of the most common file processing tasks on the web, yet virtually every existing online compression service forces users to transmit personal photos, business graphics, and sensitive scanned documents to remote cloud infrastructure. PrivacyFold's Client-Side Image Compressor re-engineers modern production-grade compression algorithms—including Mozilla's MozJPEG, Google's WebP, libpng, and AVIF—compiled directly into WebAssembly. This architecture enables industrial-strength compression with intelligent perceptual quantization, color subsampling, and binary size targeting to run entirely within your local browser sandbox. You can compress images to exact kilobyte limits (e.g. under 200 KB for portal forms) with zero server bills, zero bandwidth consumption, and guaranteed zero privacy leakage.

seo.aeoSummary: PrivacyFold's Client-Side Image Compressor runs high-performance WebAssembly builds of MozJPEG, WebP, and AVIF entirely in-browser. It reduces image payload by up to 85% with exact kilobyte targeting while maintaining complete offline data isolation.

faqs.question: How does in-browser WebAssembly image compression compare to TinyPNG or cloud compressors?
faqs.answer: PrivacyFold uses the exact same underlying compression libraries (MozJPEG and Google WebP encoders) that top cloud services use, but compiles them to WebAssembly so they execute inside your browser. You get identical or superior visual compression ratios without ever having to upload your files to a third-party server.

faqs.question: Can I specify an exact file size target like "under 250 KB" for portal uploads?
faqs.answer: Yes. The tool features an iterative binary search solver that calculates the optimal quality factor and resolution scaling to guarantee your exported file lands just under your specified kilobyte cap (e.g., 200 KB, 500 KB, or 2 MB).

faqs.question: Does compressing my images in my browser slow down my computer?
faqs.answer: No. WebAssembly runs at near-native execution speed with SIMD vectorization. Compressing a typical 5 MB smartphone photograph takes between 80 to 250 milliseconds on modern laptops and smartphones.

faqs.question: Are my original photos replaced or overwritten?
faqs.answer: Never. Browser security sandboxes prevent websites from modifying existing files on your hard drive. Your compressed image is created as a new file in your Downloads folder.

faqs.question: Can this tool convert PNG graphics with transparency into modern WebP?
faqs.answer: Yes. WebP supports full 8-bit alpha transparency while reducing file size by 30% to 70% compared to traditional 24-bit PNG files.

faqs.question: Can AI agents or automated scripts trigger client-side compression?
faqs.answer: Yes. Through the PrivacyFold programmatic SDK (`window.privacyfold.run("image_compress", { target: 200000 })`), AI agents, MCP servers, and local browser automation scripts can compress images headlessly.

steps: Drag and drop single or multiple image files (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF) into the browser workspace.
Choose a compression preset or specify an exact target size (e.g. under 500 KB or 80% quality).
Compare original and compressed images side-by-side using the real-time visual inspection slider.
Fine-tune quality, chroma subsampling, and dimension constraints.
Save your compressed images individually or as a single combined batch archive.

settingsExplained.name: Target Size Solver
settingsExplained.description: Iteratively discovers the ideal quality setting to produce a file strictly below your desired byte limit.
settingsExplained.example: Set to 256,000 bytes for UK visa uploads or 500,000 bytes for online job portals.

settingsExplained.name: Quality Factor (0.0 – 1.0)
settingsExplained.description: Controls lossy compression aggressiveness. 0.80 to 0.85 delivers visually lossless results for photographic content.
settingsExplained.example: Use 0.85 for professional portfolios; 0.70 for mobile web delivery.

settingsExplained.name: Maximum Dimension Constraint
settingsExplained.description: Scales down oversized width and height while maintaining original aspect ratio to further reduce byte payload.
settingsExplained.example: Resizes 6000x4000 camera originals down to 2000x1333 for web publishing.

whatToExpect.results: Typical size reductions of 60% to 85% for raw camera JPEGs and 40% to 70% for PNG graphics, with crisp perceptual clarity verified by structural similarity index (SSIM).
whatToExpect.limits: Supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, and GIF up to 50 MB per file.
whatToExpect.benchmarks: MozJPEG WASM encodes a 4K 12 MP photo in ~180ms in modern Chrome/Firefox with WebAssembly SIMD.

privacyProof.howItWorks: Images are decoded via native browser decoders and re-encoded using compiled WASM binaries (mozjpeg_enc.wasm and webp_enc.wasm) running in Web Workers with zero network access.
verificationSteps: Load a 10 MB image and compress to 80% quality.
Check network logs: 0 network bytes sent; total offline autonomy.
privacyProof.openSourceNotice: Built using @jsquash/mozjpeg and @jsquash/webp open source WebAssembly engines under MIT license.
